source_snapshot.procedure: Run `stress-ng --cpu 225 -t 60` for one minute, idle for one minute, and repeat for eight hours; generic setup clears logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: System remains workable after stress and no unexpected error is generated.
source_snapshot.script: Private Script Library reference whose path ends `stability-idle/idle-24-hrs`; 30 attended and 480 machine minutes.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; performs only one stress/sleep pair over password-bearing host-key-unsafe SSH, tails away output and incorrectly describes CPU+DIMM+disk stress absent from this row.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION at HIGH risk; dedicated SUT, topology-aware validation, exact schedule, per-cycle recovery/health evidence and independent recovery are required.

old_problem: The historical review treated the `idle-24-hrs` private Script path name as a competing 24-hour requirement even though the actual Procedure says eight hours and Machine Time independently says 480 minutes. It also left wall-clock versus cycle accounting unresolved. DeepSeek ran only one pair, discarded most output, added unrelated DIMM/disk scope and did not prove that all 225 workers exited or that the system recovered during each idle interval.
disposition_reason: Resolve Engineering Decision Pending and Source Conflict. The executable Procedure and numeric Machine Time independently agree on eight hours; 60 seconds stress plus 60 seconds idle repeated over 480 minutes yields 240 complete source cycles. A path label on an unavailable private script is not an authoritative instruction to triple duration and cannot override both explicit fields. The review preserves the literal 225-worker burst, 60-second stress, 60-second observed idle and full eight-hour exposure; it neither shortens to a smoke test nor substitutes a topology-derived worker count. Official stress-ng documentation confirms that `--cpu 225` selects workers and `-t 60` applies a timeout that may overrun while a worker exits, so every cycle must prove process termination and measure actual boundaries. Runtime topology suitability, limits and SUT identity are parameterized prerequisites rather than an unresolved Engineering Decision.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1769, same-row DeepSeek/test-json content, GPT V2, historical V3.1 record, original pending/conflict analyses, duplicate-code result, private-script reference and ED rules were read. The actual next missing formal queue identity was reconstructed and directly opened as Functionality row 1776 / Wistron-HW-00409-V002 / c15b08446d946ad6.

Procedure states eight hours and Machine Time is 480 minutes. One 60-second stress plus one 60-second idle pair is two minutes, so 240 complete pairs provide exactly 480 minutes of required stress/idle exposure before orchestration overhead.

The source Script cell is only a URL/path; no script content, revision or 24-hour Procedure/Criteria is present. The filename `idle-24-hrs` is retained as provenance but rejected for execution unless the owner supplies a pinned revision and review proves it implements this row's eight-hour, 240-cycle contract.
ED-16 forbids a short smoke profile from passing full coverage. This record keeps all 240 cycles; an optional calibration is labeled readiness-only and never counts toward acceptance.

The literal `--cpu 225` is retained rather than silently replaced. The owner must verify the dedicated SUT can safely run it while preserving monitoring and recovery capacity; if not, the case is runtime BLOCKED until a separately approved source correction exists.

stress-ng documents that timeout termination can take longer when a worker is uninterruptible or cleaning up. Therefore fixed cycle IDs, monotonic timestamps, worker-PID exit proof and no overlap are required; `sleep 60` alone is not idle recovery evidence.
DeepSeek's CPU+DIMM+disk risk description is not added to coverage. This row exercises CPU worker bursts and the transition to observed idle only.
No stress-ng command, private script, log clear, reboot, retry or other DUT action was executed.

test_case.test_name: Full-System Idle Stress — 240 observed CPU-burst/idle recovery cycles
test_case.purpose: Validate a dedicated SUT across 240 consecutive transitions from a 225-worker, 60-second stress-ng CPU burst to a 60-second observed idle interval, proving worker termination, idle settling, continued system usability and no new unexplained platform error over the complete eight-hour source exposure.
required_package: Exact dedicated SUT and CPU topology, pinned stress-ng version, verified ability to run the literal 225 workers while retaining independent monitoring/OOB recovery, and drained workload/maintenance approval

Reviewed 240-cycle controller using monotonic time, full stress-ng output, process-group/PID tracking, 60-second stress and 60-second measured idle intervals; the private `idle-24-hrs` script is not used unless pinned and proven equivalent
Owner-approved CPU/load/frequency/temperature/power/throttling/watchdog/event limits, interval tolerance, idle-settling oracle and abort criteria
Secure verified-host access, immutable per-cycle evidence destination, independent console/BMC health collection and recovery owner
test_case.test_command: NOT STARTED; approval required. On the dedicated drained SUT, preserve baseline CPU topology, firmware, services, temperatures/power, throttling/watchdog state and OS/BMC events. Verify stress-ng identity and perform a separately labeled readiness calibration that does not count as acceptance. After approval, execute exactly 240 numbered cycles: start the literal `stress-ng --cpu 225 -t 60` burst with complete stdout/stderr/status and monotonic timestamps; verify every stress worker/process exits without overlap; then observe a full 60-second idle interval while recording CPU/load/frequency/temperature/power and service responsiveness. At every boundary capture incremental preserved events and apply approved aborts. After cycle 240, verify stable idle, services/workload and final health. Do not use the private 24-hour-named script unless its pinned content is reviewed to implement this exact contract; do not clear logs, tail output, add DIMM/disk stress, skip/replace failed cycles or restart automatically.
test_case.expected_result: All 240 numbered cycles complete once with at least 60 seconds of CPU stress and 60 seconds of observed idle exposure per cycle, no overlapping/leaked stress worker, and complete timing/status evidence. During every idle interval the approved CPU load/frequency/power/temperature/service signals settle within their limits. No thermal/power/watchdog/throttling violation or new unexplained OS/BMC event occurs, and after the final cycle the SUT is responsive, healthy and in the approved idle/workload state.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires all 240 complete cycles, full untruncated stress-ng output and worker-exit proof, measured idle recovery for every cycle, approved limit comparisons, preserved event deltas and healthy final SUT evidence. A single pair, shortened smoke run, wall-clock stop with fewer cycles, an unreviewed 24-hour script, uptime alone, tail-only metrics, leaked/overlapping worker, missing cycle evidence, limit excursion, unexpected event or failed service/idle recovery is not PASS and is reported for engineer FAIL/BLOCKED disposition. The end user decides the verdict.
safety_gate: Require a dedicated drained SUT, maintenance approval, literal 225-worker suitability check, monitoring headroom, independent OOB recovery and immediate pre-execution confirmation.

Use one bounded process group per cycle and prove all workers exit before starting the idle interval or next burst. Stop on timeout overrun beyond approved tolerance, leakage, overlap or controller/evidence failure.
Continuously enforce approved temperature, power, frequency/throttling, watchdog, load and service limits; preserve logs instead of clearing them and keep management/monitoring responsive.
Do not silently change 225 workers, one-minute intervals, 240-cycle coverage or add CPU methods/memory/disk/I/O stress. A changed workload requires owner approval and separate traceability.
On hang, thermal/power/watchdog/event fault or failed idle settling, stop and preserve evidence. Do not retry the cycle, kill unrelated processes, reboot or power-cycle automatically.
expected_evidence: Source Key/Variant, eight-hour derivation, SUT/CPU topology, pinned stress-ng/controller hash, maintenance approval, limits and recovery readiness
Immutable 1-240 cycle ledger with monotonic stress/idle boundaries, complete stress-ng stdout/stderr/exit status, worker PIDs and verified exit/no-overlap
Per-cycle CPU/load/frequency/temperature/power/throttling/watchdog and service responsiveness, including the full observed idle interval and settling decision
Preserved baseline/incremental/final dmesg, syslog/OS events and BMC health/SEL with timestamps and abort/no-retry audit
Final stable idle, SUT/service/workload readiness, any recovery action and engineer-owned PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict
test_case.recovery: On leaked worker, overrun, hang, thermal/power/watchdog/event limit, monitoring loss or failed idle/service recovery, terminate only the tracked stress process group through the approved controller, preserve the affected and prior cycle evidence and do not restart. Allow owner-directed cooldown and service recovery; if the SUT is unresponsive, the platform owner uses the approved console/BMC recovery path and records every action. No autonomous reboot, power cycle or repeated stress is permitted.

source_conflict.reason: Procedure and Machine Time are two explicit agreeing fields that define eight hours/480 minutes. The unreviewed private path name is retained but cannot create a 24-hour requirement or be executed; 240 complete two-minute cycles preserve the explicit source coverage.

blocked.reason: The workload, count, timing, evidence, safety and recovery are now deterministic. Missing SUT identity, suitability and thresholds are normal runtime prerequisites; absence at execution time blocks the run but not the review.

Documents that a timeout is at least the requested duration and termination can be delayed by uninterruptible work or cleanup, supporting measured non-overlap and observed-idle gates.
